pr.title: recursively evaluate the constants in everything that is 'mentioned'
pr.author: RalfJung

issues.title: Const-eval errors in dead functions are optimization-dependent
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

I tried this code: [[playground]](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=nightly&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=1ffcf365aa942927bfb5f465c4dc4e99)

```rust
#![feature(inline_const)]

pub fn cause_late_error<T>() {
    const {
        panic!()
    };
}

fn main() {
    let a = 1;
    let b = 2;
    if a + b == 5 {
        cause_late_error::<()>();
    }
}
```

I expected to see this happen:

```text
error[E0080]: evaluation of `cause_late_error::<()>::{constant#0}` failed
 --> src/main.rs:7:9
  |
7 |         panic!()
  |         ^^^^^^^^ the evaluated program panicked at 'explicit panic', src/main.rs:7:9
  |
  = note: this error originates in the macro `$crate::panic::panic_2021` which comes from the expansion of the macro `panic` (in Nightly builds, run with -Z macro-backtrace for more info)

note: the above error was encountered while instantiating `fn cause_late_error::<()>`
  --> src/main.rs:13:9
   |
13 |         cause_late_error::<()>();
   |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

Instead, this happened: it compiled without any warnings.

### Meta

Playground nightly, 1.69.0-nightly (2023-01-30 001a77fac33f6560ff36)

### Related

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/85836
- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/104087
- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/106617

Potential fix:

- #122568

analysis.originalLogic: Before this change, the monomorphization collector walked only the monomorphic items that were actually used after MIR optimization and evaluated their `required_consts`. Its own documentation said that the exact set of used constants can depend on optimizations, because optimizing away dead code can remove a call that uses a failing constant. Thus a no-opt build could report a post-monomorphization const-eval failure while an optimized build silently dropped the only use and did not evaluate the failing constant.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical incorrect pipeline transformation: run optimization-level-dependent MIR optimizations first, then collect only used items. Dead-code elimination or inlining can remove the call/drop/coercion that was the sole syntactic path to an item whose `required_consts` fail. The collector then has no traversal path to that const and the optimized build bypasses the error. The correction is to record `MentionedItems` before optimizations and, in mention mode, recursively evaluate all `required_consts` of mentioned items even when they are no longer used. A minimal input pair keeps the same failing generic item and changes only whether its use remains live or is hidden behind dead code: historically the live-use program errors and the dead-use optimized program does not; after the fix both must error.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust UI programs compiled at both `-Copt-level=0` and `-O`, where a generic item contains a failing post-monomorphization constant and is reached only syntactically through dead code or through a mention that optimization can erase: a dead direct call, a `Drop`/move, a reified function pointer, a closure-to-fn-pointer coercion, a const whose value contains a function pointer, an unsizing/vtable use, an inline-asm `SymFn`, or a callee hidden behind a generic, opaque, or associated type. The relevant pre-optimization MIR mentions are `Fn(Ty)`, `Drop(Ty)`, `UnsizeCast { source_ty, target_ty }`, and `Closure(Ty)`.
analysis.summary: MentionedItems makes const-eval errors in dead/generic items independent of optimization level by gathering syntactic mentions before optimization and recursively evaluating their required constants. The source-derived bug is optimization-dependent acceptance of code whose only use of a failing constant was eliminated.
analysis.trigger: A post-monomorphization const-eval failure exists in an item that is syntactically mentioned but whose actual use can be removed by MIR optimization.
preconditions: `MentionedItems` runs before optimization-level-dependent passes and is enabled even at opt-level 0.

The collector distinguishes `CollectionMode::UsedItems` from `CollectionMode::MentionedItems`; mention mode evaluates `required_consts` and recursively processes `body.mentioned_items` without producing used items.
Mention gathering must mirror collector visiting: `Call`, `Drop`, `InlineAsmOperand::SymFn`, unsizing/`DynStar`, `ReifyFnPointer`, and `ClosureFnPointer` casts.
`MentionedItem::Fn` and `MentionedItem::Closure` record a `Ty`, not a `DefId` plus args, because a generic/opaque/associated callee may only become a `FnDef` or `Closure` after monomorphization.
Used-item traversal records `used_mentioned_items` before monomorphizing so mention processing can skip items already fully visited as used items.
pitfalls: Do not gather mentions only from constants whose type is already `ty::FnDef`; pre-monomorphization callees may be generic, opaque, or associated and may only become `FnDef` during monomorphization.
Do not classify every unsizing cast as vtable-producing. The array-to-slice/str case is excluded: `(Some(ty::Array(..)), Some(ty::Str | ty::Slice(..))) => false`.

Do not treat every remaining unsize as automatically a vtable; `visit_mentioned_item` still checks target trait/dyn-star versus source trait/dyn-star and is only interested in casts that produce a vtable.
Do not update `usage_map` for mention-only visits; the source says to update it only for used items because the usage-map logic does not like duplicate mixed mention/use entries.
Do not assert the mentioned set is a stable or soundness-critical guarantee; it is explicitly optimization-independent in intent, not stable API.
Do not let test helper generics be inlined when the goal is to retain a generic mention; the patch adds `#[inline(never)]` because inlining could monomorphize the generic helper.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI revisions so the same source is compiled both ways: `//@revisions: noopt opt`, `//@ build-fail`, `//@[noopt] compile-flags: -Copt-level=0`, `//@[opt] compile-flags: -O`, and mark the same `E0080` on the const line (not only on `noopt`). Add focused cases for direct dead calls, `Drop`/move, fn-pointer reification, closure-to-fn-pointer, const-valued fn pointers, vtable-producing unsizing, inline asm `SymFn`, and callees hidden behind generic/opaque/associated types. Mark generic helpers `#[inline(never)]` so the test exercises mention gathering rather than accidental monomorphization through inlining. Require both revisions to fail with the same primary const-eval error, and keep a build-pass negative control for dead code that does not mention a failing const.
evidence: Before doing anything, remember which items are being mentioned so that the set of items
We need to detect unsizing casts that required vtables.
They may become FnDef during monomorphization!
This fails without optimizations, so it should also fail with optimizations.
